title: Modified vascularized interpositional periosteal connective tissue graft versus xenogeneic collagen matrix for soft tissue augmentation around implant in esthetic zone (A comparative Study)
authors: Abdelmaged, H., Moustafa, A.A. & Khalil, A.A. BMC Oral Health. 2025 Dec 12;25(1):1932. doi: 10.1186/s12903-025-07345-9.
supports: Clinical study from the botiss mucoderm (porcine collagen soft-tissue matrix) literature list — the product featured in it, which is not the same as the study being about the product, so check the design and the comparator before citing it as product evidence. Authors' conclusion, verbatim: “The pedicled mVIP-CTG technique resulted in a superior increase in keratinized tissue thickness around immediate implants compared to XCM. Despite this, XCM offered advantages in terms of reduced morbidity and shorter surgical time, suggesting it remains a viable alternative in cases where patient preference or clinical limitations preclude autogenous grafting” This records what the paper says, not what a rep may say: the sales wording still has to pass the claim tiers, and a study in one indication licenses nothing in another.
